cites.quote: Doctor codes such as `D-0001` are display codes derived from row ids, not stored.
System lists normally answer `20 per page`; this endpoint is a stated exception.
The day schedule of one doctor and date is served from `api/src/routes/doctors.ts`.
A doctor, patient, department or specialization kept for history but not offered for new use.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason; its slot becomes free again.
Given two doctors with the same full name and the same earliest slot start, when staff call the endpoint, then the one with the lower id comes first.
Given two doctors with the same full name and no FREE slot in the window, when staff call the endpoint, then both come last and the one with the lower id comes first.
with `doctor id as the final tie-break`

findings.suggested_fix: Use names that differ only in case, with the higher id holding the name that sorts first case-sensitively (id 5 'Dr. Kim', id 3 'dr. kim'). Expect id 3 first, or say the fixture must not return rows in id order.
findings.text: S-3 AC3 and AC5 use two doctors with the exact same name. If there is no id tie-break, rows read in insertion order (lower id first) still pass. So these ACs may not catch a missing id tie-break.

cites.quote: Specializations already have their own router in `api/src/routes/specializations.ts`.
`No other endpoint, page or booking rule changes`.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-6 AC: GET /api/specializations returns the same response before and after the change.
findings.text: S-6 checks that the day schedule and booking are unchanged, but not the existing specializations endpoints. Those share the router the new route will most likely join, so they are the nearest regression risk under REQ-16.

rubric_items.reason: S-1 to S-6 trace all 17 known REQs (REQ-1 to REQ-17). The intent has no assumed REQs.
Privacy (S-5) and no-change (S-6) are now separate stories. S-4 still puts the unpaged list together with the empty, 404 and 400 answers.

Previous F-1, F-2 and F-3 are fixed. The case, window-boundary, time-zone and Cancelled ACs now catch the likely wrong implementations. One gap: the same-name id tie-break ACs (S-3 AC3, AC5) may pass on insertion order alone.
Every value is example data or derived inline: the 21st doctor from 20 per page, 09:30 local = 04:00Z from UTC+05:30, today+6 = 2026-10-25. C1 now says the offset comes from the fixed IANA zone.
The frontmatter and body agree. FREE/BOOKED/PAST are used the same way throughout, and the derivations and wrong-implementation contrasts are written out inline.
